frames.narration: Phones count clicks per 10 second window by event time. Events arrive in this order: 1, 3, 12, 8, 5, 14. The watermark is the newest event time minus 5 seconds.
The window operator assigns each event by its event time: [0,10) holds 1, 3, 8, 5 and [10,20) holds 12, 14. After 14 the watermark is 14 - 5 = 9, below the end of [0,10), so nothing fires.
Event 22 arrives. The watermark moves to 22 - 5 = 17, which is past the end of [0,10).
The window [0,10) fires with a count of 4 and its state is dropped. [10,20) is still open: 17 is below 20.
Late but not too late: 11 arrives after 22. Its window [10,20) is still open, so it is counted (3). Then 25 moves the watermark to 20 and [10,20) fires with 3.

A phone leaves a tunnel and uploads a click with event time 9. Its window [0,10) already fired at watermark 17, so the click is late. It goes to a side output or is dropped, and the emitted 4 stays as it is.

More events: 31, 18, 35, 27. Event 18 (window [10,20)) is also late, 27 arrives after the watermark reached 30 and is late too. The sink now shows 4 and 3 for the first two windows and the count is wrong by the 3 late clicks seen so far (9, 18, 27).

The trade-off: with a delay of 20 seconds nothing in this data would be late, but every result would wait 20 seconds longer. With a delay of 0, 7 of the 16 events are late. The delay is a bet on how late the tail of your events can be.
